title: The Jio IPO
summary:
Mukesh Ambani first promised a Jio listing in 2019. In 2020, Facebook, Google and other global investors bought big stakes in Jio Platforms. The listing then slipped year after year, most recently when war in West Asia unsettled markets in 2026.

The regulator cleared the draft prospectus on 28 August 2026. The issue was made up only of new shares, mostly to repay debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm, and at an upper price of 1,119 rupees it was a record offer of about 30,200 crore rupees. It closed on 23 October booked 22.19 times. The shares listed on 28 October and closed that day about 26.7 percent above the issue price, making Jio India's second most valuable company. In the second session they climbed further, to about 33 percent above the issue price and a market value of about 13.7 lakh crore rupees. On the thirtieth, in its first results as a listed company, Jio reported a September-quarter profit of 8,389 crore rupees, up about 14 percent, on revenue of 40,475 crore rupees.
watch: Jio's shares trade for the first time after its results on Monday, the second of November, and Mint says Reliance and Jio will both be in focus. Watch how the market reads the 14 percent profit growth and the rise in revenue per user, any word on tariff increases, and whether PhonePe, Flipkart and others follow Jio to the market.

timeline.title: Ambani first promises a Jio listing
timeline.text: At the Reliance annual general meeting, Mukesh Ambani said Jio and Reliance Retail would move towards a stock market listing. He gave a time frame of within the next five years. This is where the Jio IPO story begins.

timeline.title: Facebook buys nearly 10 percent of Jio
timeline.text: Facebook agreed to invest 43,574 crore rupees in Jio Platforms. That bought it a stake of 9.99 percent. The deal valued Jio Platforms at about 4.62 lakh crore rupees, and it set off a wave of global investment into the company.

timeline.title: Google takes a 7.73 percent stake
timeline.text: At the next annual general meeting, Ambani announced that Google would invest 33,737 crore rupees in Jio Platforms. Google would get a stake of 7.73 percent. Bloomberg later noted that a listing would give big global investors like these a way to exit.

timeline.title: Reuters: no Jio IPO in 2025
timeline.text: Reuters reported that Jio would not list in 2025, citing people familiar with the matter. The sources said Jio first wanted more revenue and more subscribers. Analysts already valued the company at more than 100 billion dollars.

timeline.title: Ambani targets a listing by mid 2026
timeline.text: At the Reliance annual general meeting, Ambani said Jio aimed to list in the first half of 2026. He said Jio was making all arrangements to file for its IPO. He did not say how big a stake would be sold.

timeline.title: Jio weighs selling a 2.5 percent stake
timeline.text: Reuters reported that Jio was considering floating about 2.5 percent of the company. That depended on a proposed rule change that would let very large companies sell a smaller slice. The offer could be worth more than 4 billion dollars, and the brokerage Jefferies had valued Jio at about 180 billion dollars.

timeline.title: War in West Asia clouds the timeline
timeline.text: A report from the research firm CreditSights said the Jio listing could slip to the second half of the financial year, between October 2026 and March 2027. The reason was rising tension in West Asia. That meant the target of the first half of 2026 was likely to be missed.

timeline.title: Jio switches to an all new share issue
timeline.text: Bloomberg reported that Jio had slowed its preparations as markets fell about 9 percent below pre war levels. Jio dropped the plan to let existing shareholders sell their stakes. Instead, the IPO would only issue new shares.

timeline.title: Draft prospectus filed at the annual meeting
timeline.text: At the Reliance annual general meeting, Ambani said the Jio board had approved the draft red herring prospectus. It was filed with the market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the same day. The plan was a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares.

timeline.title: Market regulator clears the IPO
timeline.text: The market regulator issued its observation letter on the draft prospectus, which clears the way for the offer. Early estimates put the issue at around 37,700 crore rupees. The draft prospectus said about 27,500 crore rupees would repay borrowings of Reliance Jio Infocomm.

timeline.title: Reports point to an October 21 opening
timeline.text: Citing Moneycontrol, reports said the offer would likely open on 21 October and list on 28 October. Most of the money would go to repay about 27,500 crore rupees of Reliance Jio Infocomm debt. Pricing and valuation were still not decided.

timeline.title: Price band set for a record offer
timeline.text: Jio filed its final prospectus and set a price band of 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share. At the top of the band, the offer raises about 30,200 crore rupees, the largest IPO in India. Up to 2,500 crore rupees is set aside for Reliance shareholders, and up to 500 crore rupees for employees. Reuters said the top price values Jio at around 10.3 lakh crore rupees.

timeline.title: Anchor investors put in 8,110 crore rupees
timeline.text: Jio raised about 8,110 crore rupees from 212 anchor investors, all at the top price of 1,119 rupees. Bids reportedly topped 2.5 lakh crore rupees, around 30 times the shares on offer. Investors included Singapore's government, the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Norway's sovereign fund, while Life Insurance Corporation got about 500 crore rupees of shares.

timeline.title: Brokerages weigh in on the eve of the IPO
timeline.text: On the eve of the offer, Mint reported that the brokerage Motilal Oswal rated the issue subscribe, both for listing gains and for the long term. It pointed to Jio's market leadership and growth in broadband and enterprise services. Allotment is expected on 26 October, with listing on 28 October.

timeline.title: The offer opens to the public
timeline.text: The Jio Platforms offer opened for subscription, aiming to raise about 30,213 crore rupees through a fresh issue of 27 crore shares. It was fully subscribed within about 100 minutes, the fastest of India's mega issues, and ended day one booked 3.16 times. Big institutions bid for 9.42 times their quota, but retail investors took only 0.73 times theirs. The Economic Times put day one bids at about 70,000 crore rupees, ahead of the LIC and NSE issues.

timeline.title: Retail quota filled on day two
timeline.text: On day two, the offer was subscribed 5.57 times, up from 3.16 times on day one. Big institutions bid for 13.29 times their quota, non-institutional investors for 5.97 times and retail investors for 1.54 times, so the retail portion was filled. Moneycontrol put total demand at about 3.73 lakh crore rupees, with about 2.5 lakh crore rupees of it from institutions.

timeline.title: Bidding closes at 22 times, a string of records
timeline.text: The offer closed on Friday subscribed 22.19 times. Big institutions bid for about 70.6 times their quota, and retail investors for about 2.7 times theirs. Mint put total bids at about 4.72 lakh crore rupees, and Moneycontrol said it was the first IPO anywhere to draw more than one crore applications. At about 30,200 crore rupees, it overtakes Hyundai Motor India as the country's biggest offer.

timeline.title: Grey market points to a listing gain
timeline.text: Over the weekend, Mint reported a grey market premium of about 250 rupees a share. On that basis it suggested a possible listing price of about 1,369 rupees, roughly 22 percent above the top of the band. Allotment was set for Monday, the twenty-sixth, through the registrar KFin Technologies, with listing on the NSE and BSE planned for Wednesday, the twenty-eighth, at 10 in the morning. Applicants who get no shares will have their blocked money released, and one lot of 12 shares costs 13,428 rupees at the top price.

timeline.title: Allotment done, and a modest bankers' fee
timeline.text: Share allotment was finalised on Monday, and successful applicants were due to get their shares in their demat accounts on Tuesday, the twenty-seventh. The Economic Times and Business Standard reported that Jio is paying its 19 banks about 196 crore rupees in fees, only 0.65 percent of the issue. Hyundai Motor India paid about 493 crore rupees, or 1.77 percent, on a smaller offer. Mint said a single lot would be worth about 16,428 rupees at the grey market's implied listing price, a gain of about 3,000 rupees.

timeline.title: Listing day: a 27 percent jump
timeline.text: On the morning of the listing, Business Standard said the grey market put Jio about 22 percent above the issue price, and Mint said market watchers saw a gain of up to about 25 percent. Moneycontrol said bids for the issue had topped 7 lakh crore rupees, and that Jio's market value could pass 10.3 lakh crore rupees. Nomura began coverage with a buy rating and a target of 1,340 rupees, nearly 20 percent above the issue price, citing tariff hikes, home broadband growth and better free cash flow. The debut came on a weak morning, with the Sensex down more than 650 points at the open. By the close, the shares had ended at 1,417.35 rupees, about 26.7 percent above the issue price. That made Jio the second most valuable company in India, ahead of Bharti Airtel, with a market value of more than 13 lakh crore rupees. It lifted the Reliance group past the Tata group as the country's most valuable business house, and the Economic Times said it put Jio among the five biggest telecom companies in the world. Three more brokers began coverage: Motilal Oswal and Elara Capital with buy ratings, and Dolat Capital with an accumulate rating and a target that points to about 28 percent upside.

timeline.title: Second session: gains stretch to 33 percent
timeline.text: On its second day of trading, Jio's shares rose as much as 5 percent, according to Business Standard, taking the stock about 33 percent above the issue price of 1,119 rupees and its market value to about 13.7 lakh crore rupees. Bloomberg, writing in Business Standard, said the strong debut has lifted confidence in India's listing pipeline, with 113 companies cleared to list and another 115 that have filed draft papers. Names such as PhonePe, Flipkart and Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages could follow.

timeline.title: First results as a listed company
timeline.text: Jio Platforms reported its first quarterly results since listing. Net profit for the September quarter rose about 14 percent from a year ago to 8,389 crore rupees, and revenue grew about 11 percent to 40,475 crore rupees, according to the Economic Times and Mint. Average revenue per user rose to 218 rupees 80 paise, and the company added 9.1 million subscribers, taking its base to 542.4 million. Business Standard also reported that retail investors had borrowed about 234 million dollars in margin funding to trade Jio on its debut day.
